title: Try it, for me, for yourself
goal: Add a shade to a verb with the helpers görmek (try), bermek (for someone) and almak (for yourself).

intro.text: After `-(Y)p`, *görmek* is **try it and see**: *Okap gör!* (give it a read!). *Bermek* is **for someone**: *Maňa ýazyp ber* (write it down for me). *Almak* is **for yourself**: *Ýazyp al* (write it down, to keep). The helper takes the tense and the person: *okap gördüm*, *ýazyp beriň*.

exercises.question: How do you say **try this shirt on**?

why.1: *Bermek* is **for someone**: put it on for someone else.

exercises.explain: *geýip gör*: put it on and see. *Görmek* after `-(Y)p` is **try it**.

reject.why: *Dadyp ber* would be **taste it for someone**. Try it and see: *dadyp gör*.
*Almak* is **for yourself**, to keep. Try it and see: *dadyp gör*.

exercises.explain: *dadyp gör*: taste it and see what you think.

reject.why: *Ýazyp al* is **write it down for yourself**. **For me**: *ýazyp ber*.

exercises.explain: *ýazyp ber*: write it **for me**. *Maňa* says who it's for.

exercises.label: *alyp bermek* (to buy for someone) in the past: I bought (for…), you bought…
exercises.explain: *Alyp* never changes; the helper *bermek* takes the past: *berdim, berdiň, berdi…*

accept: [Dad|My dad|My father] bought a phone for me.
[Dad|My dad|My father] got me a phone.

exercises.question: *Telefon nomerimi ýazyp al.* Who keeps the number?

why.1: That would be *Maňa ýazyp ber*: write it **for me**.
why.2: *Ýazmak* is to write: it's written down.

exercises.explain: *Almak* after `-(Y)p` is **for yourself**: you write it down so you have it.

exercises.prompt: Have you ever ridden a camel?
exercises.explain: In the past, *-(Y)p görmek* asks **have you ever (tried it)?**: *münüp gördüňmi?*

exercises.en: The teacher explained the rule to us.

reject.why: *Almak* is **for oneself**. The teacher did it **for us**: *düşündirip berdi*.

exercises.explain: *düşündirip berdi*: explained it **for us**, as a favour.

exercises.prompt: Men ony çözüp gördüm, ýöne başarmadym.
accept: I tried to solve it, but I could not.
I tried [to solve|solving] it, but I [did not manage|did not manage to|failed|could not do it].
I tried solving it, but I could not.
I tried to solve it but did not manage.

exercises.explain: *görkezip beriň*: show it **for me**, politely. The plain *görkeziň* is right too.

exercises.question: Which means **I tasted it to see what it was like**?

why.1: *Iýmäge synanyşdym*: I tried to eat it, I made an effort.

exercises.explain: *-(Y)p görmek*: try it and see. *Synanyşmak*: make an effort.

exercises.title: Kerim palaw bişirýär
exercises.passage:
Kerim türkmen naharlaryny gowy görýär, ýöne bişirip bilmeýär. Geçen hepde ol Aýnalara myhmançylyga bardy. Aýnanyň ejesi myhmanlara palaw bişirip berdi. Kerim palawy dadyp gören badyna, onuň örän tagamlydygyny aýtdy.

Nahardan soň, Aýnanyň ejesi oňa palawyň reseptini düşündirip berdi. Kerim hemme zady depderine ýazyp aldy. Öýe gelenden soň, ol palaw bişirip gördi. Ilki başarmady, ýöne gaýtalap-gaýtalap bişirip, ahyrynda öwrendi.
exercises.translation: Kerim loves Turkmen food, but he can't cook. Last week he went visiting at Aýna's. Aýna's mother made palaw for the guests. As soon as Kerim tasted the palaw, he said it was delicious. After the meal, Aýna's mother explained the recipe to him. Kerim wrote everything down in his notebook. After getting home, he tried making palaw. At first he couldn't manage, but by cooking it again and again, he finally learned.

questions.q: Who made the palaw for the guests?
questions.explain: *Aýnanyň ejesi myhmanlara palaw bişirip berdi*: she made it for them.

options: Kerim wrote it down for himself
Kerim wrote it down for Aýna's mother

questions.q: Did Kerim manage it the first time?
options: no, but he learned by cooking it again and again
questions.explain: *Ilki başarmady, ýöne gaýtalap-gaýtalap bişirip, ahyrynda öwrendi.*
